How Much Do Feet Pics Sell For?

The sticker price and the money that reaches you are different numbers. A $30 set on a shop that takes 15 percent is not a $30 payday, and a month of zero sales is still a possible month.

Dark-Ero editorialUpdated 2026-11-1018+

At a glance

Single images commonly list at $5 to $15, and five-image sets at $20 to $40.

Custom work is priced higher because it is labour, not a file you already shot.

Beginner totals people report are often $50 to $200 in month one, and plenty of people report less.

Key takeaways

  • Ten-image sets often list at $40 to $75, and a custom ten-image set at $60 to $150.
  • Custom video is often priced per minute, in a band around $50 to $200.
  • FeetFinder takes 15 percent on Basic or 10 percent on Premium, on top of the plan.
  • Snifffr takes no cut of the sale and charges Premium to message and cash out.
  • Self-reported incomes are not a platform average, so do not budget your rent on them.

In 2026, single feet pics commonly sell for $5 to $15, and a five-image set for $20 to $40. A ten-image set often lists at $40 to $75, with custom sets and custom video above those bands.

The platform-by-platform version of those ranges is how much feet pics sell for. The figures come from listed prices and from creator-disclosed logs, not from a shop publishing its average seller.

How a month is actually built, once a price exists, is in how to make money selling feet pics. Consistency and repeat buyers move the total more than a slightly braver sticker.

Disclosure: Dark-Ero is independent, with no affiliate link on this page. Adults 18+ only.

What listings ask

A $5 single is the floor many sellers list at, and a lone image is a less common product than a set. Volume discounts mean the per-image price falls as the set gets bigger, which is normal retail, not a mistake.

A custom ten-image set, with poses and props the buyer names, often lists at $60 to $150 because you are shooting to order. Custom video is cleaner as a per-minute rate, and sellers often quote $50 to $200 a minute, with sound adding more.

Worn socks and similar items sit in a different band, often higher per parcel and lower in volume. Tips can match a set for someone with regulars, and they are rare for a seller who has not built those relationships yet.

Subscription pages, where a shop allows them, turn one monthly price into a year of access. The same files can still be sold again as separate items, which is why a $10 subscription and a $30 set are not rivals so much as two products.

What each shop takes

FeetFinder adds a plan fee and then 15 percent on Basic or 10 percent on Premium, so you keep 85 or 90 percent of the sale. Sets there often list from $5 to $50, and the plan details are in our FeetFinder review.

The outside fee check is the FeetFinder review. Basic is $4.99 a month, $14.99 a year or $40 lifetime, and Premium is $14.99 a month, $49.99 a year or $80 lifetime.

Snifffr takes no commission on the sale and instead charges Premium, put at $12.95 every 30 days in a November 2026 fee check, which you need in order to message, accept deals and cash out. Sellers receive $1 per token, cash out through Wise from a 10-token minimum once they are verified, and the terms require the payment to stay inside a deal.

Our write-up of that gate is the Snifffr review. Observed sock listings in the source check sat around $40 to $120 for a pair worn several days, which is a different product from a $10 photo.

The ranking site's Snifffr pass is the Snifffr review. Older FAQ lines that talk about paying the seller directly lose to the current terms, so follow the terms.

Fun With Feet charges a listing fee and says it takes no commission, with the seller FAQ at $9.99 for one month or $14.99 for three months. Withdrawals start at a $50 balance, and a comparison page on the same site has quoted different plan lengths, so the FAQ figure is the one to recheck at signup.

OnlyFans takes 20 percent, and creators keep 80 percent of earnings. Foot creators there are competing with the whole catalogue, which our OnlyFans review treats as a discovery problem rather than a fee surprise.

All Things Worn is built around worn items, joins free, and lists Premium Seller at $19.99 every 30 days or $69.99 for six months with no commission. Its own used-panties page puts typical prices at $20 to $40 or more.

Direct sales keep the sticker and hand you the fraud risk, the processor fee and the tax filing. If the pitch is that a shop fee is theft, read where to sell feet pics for free before you leave the checkout that can reverse a charge.

What people say they earn

Creator-disclosed logs, not a platform report, are where the monthly bands come from. Beginners on FeetFinder commonly describe $50 to $200 in the first month, sellers a few months in describe $500 to $2,500, and a smaller group with a year of branding describes $3,000 to $15,000.

The shop does not publish that distribution, and the loud posts are the ones that get screenshotted. A month of nothing is compatible with every one of those bands, because the bands describe people who posted a number, not people who stayed quiet.

Established foot creators on OnlyFans are described in a similarly wide band, from a few hundred dollars to well into five figures, and the top of it takes a year of brand, not a weekend. The honest setup is how to make money selling feet pics.

Before you chase a price that attracts the wrong buyers, read how to sell feet pics without getting scammed. Free samples and off-platform payments are how a high sticker turns into no money.

The ranked fee list on this site is best sites to sell feet pics. Compare the plan plus the percentage at the sales you actually expect.

Fun With Feet's listing-fee maths is easier to see in the Fun With Feet review. A zero commission with a quiet shop can cost more than 15 percent on a shop that has buyers.

When you want the front doors in one place, use feet marketplaces. Price the work you can repeat, then raise it after reviews exist.

Verdict

Ask $5 to $15 for a single, $20 to $40 for a small set, and more when the buyer is commissioning your time. Then subtract the plan and the percentage before you tell anyone what you made.

Reported months are stories, not a wage. Adults only, and a shop that will not show its fee on the checkout is the one to leave.

FAQ

How much does a single feet pic sell for?

Sellers commonly list singles at $5 to $15. A set is the more usual product, and the per-image price drops as the set gets larger.

How much is a feet pic set?

A five-image set often lists at $20 to $40, and a ten-image set at $40 to $75. Custom sets of about ten images often run $60 to $150.

What do beginners actually make?

Self-reported first months on FeetFinder often fall between $50 and $200, and some sellers make nothing while they learn the shop. Those figures are not an official average.

How much does FeetFinder take?

Basic keeps 85 percent of the sale and Premium keeps 90 percent, after you have paid the plan. The plan is charged even in a month with no sales.

Does Snifffr take a percentage?

Snifffr takes no cut of the sale and charges a Premium membership to message and cash out. A November 2026 check put that membership at $12.95 every 30 days, so confirm it at checkout.

Can I trust a $10,000 month I saw online?

Treat it as one person's claim unless the shop published it. The upper band exists in self-reports, and it is a poor budget for a first month.
